whole:
THE QUESTION, FROZEN. Of the planning skill's draft (Planning file 1: SKILL.md and freezing, splits, readers-and-markers, changes, owner - the loaned testing-against-cases is judged in the HV project), for each rule and paragraph: what in the HV Skill's record holds it, quoted; what fails if it is removed; whether a near neighbour would do as well. The range is the record the draft names - HV plans H56, H58, H61, H63, H67, H68, results H57, H59, H62, H64, the project story H55 to H67, Lessons, Decisions, and RESEARCH-CONVENTIONS.md. The kind of question is "does it achieve its purpose", and the purpose the draft sets itself is the one in its second paragraph: "Every rule below was used in one project's record before it was written here. None is new."

WHERE THE JOBS CAME FROM. Two jobs are the owner's (given): a skill that chooses and never judges (H5, H6), and the freeze (H6, "Harden HV and planning right now, freeze them"). One is fixed and outside the test: the owner's word before every phase, and the model bars (decisions 38, H4, H7). Every other job I tested - that each rule have a case behind it, that a near neighbour do worse, that the draft carry what the record used - is added by me from the task and from the skill's own procedure. Parts held only by those are marked accordingly.

FLIP. Would these rules have been written the same had the record come out the other way - breaks recurring everywhere, agreement low? For most of them, yes, and that is the central finding: they are procedure, and their provenance is the root conventions plus one project's habits, not any outcome. Only nine parts were written because something failed and the failure is recorded: the authority diff (Lesson 44), the empty-return rule (Lesson 45), printing every hit (Lesson 46), the owner's word (Lesson 40), the frozen mid-plan observation (H56 into H57), the blind second marker and agreement by field (plan 52's stated flaw into H63/H64), the tool audit (H61 into H62), stranger-applicable criteria (H64's struck field), and reading the record rather than a memory of it (Lesson 48). Those are built. The rest are fitted to one history, and three are asserted.

DIRECTION. The draft runs backwards from the record: it was written by reading the plans and naming what they had in common. That is honest and it is also the weakest form of holding, in the skill's own words - "Tuned by trial and survival on past cases. It is held in place exactly where it was tested." Poking the record moves the draft; poking the draft moves nothing yet, because nothing has been run under it.

THE ANSWER IN THE STARTING POINTS. One hand wrote the plans, the results, the marks, the changes and this draft. The jobs (what a plan must contain) and the parts (the rules) come from the same source, so their fit proves nothing - the trap the skill names as "Marking your own jobs as the owner's" and "Passing your own test". The record contains exactly one independent check of anything: the Sonnet second marker of H63/H64, and it disagreed enough to strike three fields and to find the first marker wrong twice. No comparable check has touched the planning rules. Worse, the draft's own first test repeats the pattern it was built to catch: P2's marker is "the first marker, by eye, against the skill's own checklist", and its prediction 1 asserts "H67 carries all eleven" items of a checklist abstracted from H67 - a half that cannot fail, which the draft's own watch-item ("A plan that cannot fail") forbids.

PAIRS THAT PULL. Three, each with a side that gives way in the record and no side named in the draft. (1) "A break seen once forces a repeat, not a change" against "one change answers every open fault at once": H67 bundles five faults of which H62's two were seen in one run each and never repeated ("Not tested: whether the two new faults recur"), so bundling won. (2) The held-out set "spent once a version is judged on it" against "then the same test again under the new file": H67 names the loser ("Any version but 32 on the held-out set: it is spent on 32 once marked"). (3) readers-and-markers.md's absolute Fable 5.1 bar against owner.md's permission-gated one: decisions H4 and H7 make the absolute right, so owner.md gives way. The third is the one that matters, because it is a safety rule stated at two strengths inside one skill.

CATCH-ALLS AND GAUGES. "Traps" is a required section in every plan and every results file of the record and in the draft's report shape, and nothing says what would show a trap list is swallowing a job. The record does carry the gauge for the one place it matters - plan 52's five failure conditions, against which file 54 marked itself, including an honest "partly" - and the draft drops exactly that. So the draft's missing failure conditions and its ungauged traps are one fault, and edit 7 closes both.

WHAT THE CHANGE LIST LEAVES OUT. Everything except one project. One skill under test (the HV skill, in three versions), two readers (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash; Sonnet 5 through a subagent transport whose model id H61 records as "expected, not verified"), one corpus, two sources carrying all the repeat evidence, one marker pair, one owner, documents made of words. Never tested: a claim, a workflow, a human marker, a third reading, an answer-keyed run, a freeze, the reserve, the held-out 33, and the skill itself (INDEX: "Tested by - Not yet"). The draft's front matter claims reach over "a claim, a skill or a workflow" and the record supports one of the three.

RIVALS. The strongest rival to the whole draft is "RESEARCH-CONVENTIONS.md plus the loaned module, and nothing else". It is not idle against that rival: the conventions contain nothing about the plan-contents list, counts against rates, printing every hit, the authority diff, the tool audit, arms never summed, the repeat-before-change rule, the fitting/held-out/reserve split, blind second marking with agreement read by field, or the results-file shape. Remove the draft and those go. But roughly the whole first paragraph of readers-and-markers.md, all of step 4, most of step 5, "what was not tested named" and "a change is a new numbered file" are the conventions restated, and are marked borrowed rather than held. The draft's real increment is smaller than it looks and is precisely what P2 should test.

VERDICT, plainly. The draft is a faithful and mostly well-anchored abstraction of one project's practice. Seventeen parts are held, nine of them by a recorded failure that shows what goes wrong without them - the strongest being Lesson 46 (ten claims wrong, fixed by printing every hit), Lesson 44 (a part-spent pilot, fixed by the diff before every call), Lesson 40 (thirty agents launched, fixed by the owner's word) and H56's frozen observation (a misaimed change caught before the run that would have licensed it). Eleven parts are borrowed from the root conventions or from the HV skill and are held there, not here. Two are held if a plan that has never run is the live one (the freeze; the reserve). One is unknown (the third reading). Several are duplicated across files as two routes to one job. Three rules are contradicted by the record they cite: "Counts, never rates" (H63 froze a rate and H64 reported one), "A break seen once forces a repeat, not a change" (H57 made change 1 without a recurrence, on the plan's rule), and "three repeats per box is the least that separates a wording fault from a run" (H57 and H60 say it separates nothing). Two numbers and one qualifier are asserted with nothing behind them: "five is the least a judgment rests on" (absent from the whole repository), and step 7's "where the faults share a cause" (H67 answered five unrelated faults in one file). Two rules the record used are missing: the marker's three layers with the layer at fault named on every report (plan 52, and H64 caught a marker error with it), and the test's own failure conditions written before the run and marked after (plan 52 and file 54; also plans 42 and 49). One router row is narrower than the module it points at, one ledger the draft points to does not exist, and one clause (the Opus 5 permission, citing decision H7) falsifies the front-matter claim that every rule was used in the record before being written here - and, on the modification order of the files, suggests that this numbered authority file was edited after its own test plan was frozen, with no log entry, against both the root conventions and the project's own rule.

WHAT WOULD MAKE IT HARDER TO VARY, the two things worth most. (1) Put a blind second marker on P2. P2's only marker is the one who wrote the skill, which is the exact conflict plan 52 named and H63/H64 measured, and the script and procedure already exist (second_marker.py, the shuffle, the closed mapping, agreement by field). Without it, P2 can show that a reader with the skill produces a plan; it cannot show that the plan is better, and its own prediction 1 half cannot fail. (2) Take one rule out and re-derive a recorded plan without it. The record has one such case and it is the most convincing thing in the draft (H56's frozen observation catching a misaimed change). A second - for instance, re-mark six H57 reports with the layer rule removed, and count what changes - would move a rule from fitted to built, which is the only kind of holding that says anything about the cases the draft has not met.

ONE NEXT STEP. Before P2 runs, add the blind second marker of the plans to it as an addendum written first and naming what it gives up (the H61 pattern), since P2's "What this does not test" already names its absence.
